rejection.symptom: The key contract included the complete ordered reversible history while the same experiment required ordinary transposition hits and cutoffs.
rejection.false_inference: A fully path-specific ordered history key could still identify a position reached through a different move order as the same transposition.
rejection.cause: Different paths necessarily contain different ordered intermediate states, so the frozen key separates every legitimate path transposition by design.
rejection.prevention: Require a semantic-equivalence and reuse-equivalence proof before freezing a TT context key; use a separately preregistered bounded history abstraction rather than changing an immutable contract in place.

This rejection does not alter the closed alpha-beta or clocked-iterative results.
